originalTitle: 'Insufficient funds' to pay Brewdog creditors after takeover deal
summary: Administrators say about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and holiday pay and £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.
content:
Aberdeenshire-based Brewdog had more than £500m of debts when it was sold

Several creditors of collapsed Scottish beer giant Brewdog are not expected to receive anything from the administration process.

A report from administrators AlixPartners said there were "insufficient funds" for payouts from Brewdog's retail arm - including £2.4m owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

Brewdog had also owed £489,000 for wages and holiday pay, which will not be paid through the administration process. Staff have instead received compensation from the UK government's Insolvency Service.

The Aberdeenshire-based brewer had more than £500m of debts when it was sold in March to US drinks firm Tilray in a £33m rescue deal.

From a £1bn dream to a brutal collapse: How Brewdog hit the rocks

BrewDog's takeover saw 38 bars close across the UK and £20m in unpaid bills left to hundreds of UK businesses .

Unpaid businesses ranged from coffee shops, bakeries and laundry services, to lawyers, councils and holiday parks.

Creditors included West Ham United FC, Lord's Cricket Ground and Manchester University.

AlixPartners said there were now "insufficient funds" for preferential creditors to be repaid.

This is due to lower than expected funds raised through sales of Brewdog assets and increased costs during the administration period.

Martin Dickie and James Watt founded Brewdog in 2007

The administrators cited unforeseen costs around the security of closed Brewdog pubs after a number of "unauthorised occupiers" gained access.

AlixPartners said it worked with landlords and lawyers to remove them.

The report highlights small amounts of money raised through asset sales. These include:

A 7.8 acre field in Potterton, Aberdeenshire, which sold to a local farmer for £41,300

Nine Brewdog vehicles of "old age and varying roadworthiness" that made only £6,250 from just one sale. The rest were abandoned.

A settlement involving drinks equipment sold to Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lords, which generated £62,000.

Are you a Brewdog creditor or worker affected by this? What impact has it had?

Parent company BrewDog PLC is still expected to pay its preferential creditor, HMRC, in full for £3.66m tax owed - mainly VAT and excise duty.

Brewdog's biggest debt was to financial services group HSBC, which was owed more than £61m across various banking arms.

It has recovered tens of millions of pounds, but still faces an estimated shortfall of £16.8m.

The report noted that this could be reduced through asset sales in the United States.

Private equity backer TSG, which took a 22% stake in the brewer in 2017, is set to lose £27.6m.

Brewdog also owes around £190m to unsecured creditors. They are expected to receive less than a penny in the pound of what they are owed.

Brewdog's collapse brought the immediate closure of 38 UK pubs

In March 440 staff were made redundant and 736 employees transferred to Tilray, after the US firm bought Brewdog's brand and UK operation.

Redundant staff can claim for unpaid wages through the government's Insolvency Service. AlixPartners said workers were given information on this support.

Eleven bars were retained as part of the sale while 38 other pubs closed immediately.

Brewdog's collapse also rendered the shares of about 200,000 crowdfunding investors worthless.

Earlier this year, Alixpartners confirmed that investors in the Equity for Punks scheme would get no return on their shares.

Investors typically spent about £500 on shares - although others invested much larger sums - in return for a stake in the company, discounts and perks.

The administrators stated these shares now had "no value".

Brewdog, which was founded in 2007 by friends James Watt and Martin Dickie, had four breweries and about 100 pubs across the world at its peak.

Watt said he was "heartbroken" after the collapse and apologised to staff and investors.

Brewdog's owner Tilray has been approached for comment.

chineseTitle: 收购交易后“资金不足”支付 Brewdog 债权人
chineseSummary: 管理人员表示，公司欠员工工资和假期工资约 489,000 英镑，欠英国税务海关总署 240 万英镑未付增值税。
chineseContent:
总部位于阿伯丁郡的 Brewdog 在出售时负债超过 5 亿英镑

倒闭的苏格兰啤酒巨头 Brewdog 的几位债权人预计不会从行政程序中获得任何好处。

管理人员 AlixPartners 的一份报告称，Brewdog 零售部门的支出“资金不足”，其中包括欠英国税务海关总署 (HMRC) 的 240 万英镑未付增值税。

Brewdog 还欠下 489,000 英镑的工资和假期工资，这些费用将不会通过行政程序支付。相反，工作人员从英国政府破产服务处获得了补偿。

这家总部位于阿伯丁郡的啤酒制造商在 3 月份以 3300 万英镑的救助协议被出售给美国饮料公司 Tilray 时，负债超过 5 亿英镑。

从 10 亿英镑的梦想到残酷的崩溃：Brewdog 如何触礁

BrewDog 的收购导致英国 38 家酒吧关闭，数百家英国企业欠下 2000 万英镑的未付账单。

无薪企业的范围从咖啡店、面包店和洗衣服务，到律师、议会和假日公园。

债权人包括西汉姆联队、罗德板球场和曼彻斯特大学。

AlixPartners表示，目前“资金不足”可供优先债权人偿还。

这是由于通过出售 Brewdog 资产筹集的资金低于预期以及管理期间成本增加。

Martin Dickie 和 James Watt 于 2007 年创立了 Brewdog

管理人员指出，在一些“未经授权的占用者”进入后，关闭的 Brewdog 酒吧的安全造成了不可预见的成本。

AlixPartners 表示，它与房东和律师合作将其拆除。

该报告强调了通过资产出售筹集的少量资金。这些包括：

阿伯丁郡波特顿的一块 7.8 英亩的田地，以 41,300 英镑的价格卖给了当地农民

九辆 Brewdog 车“年代久远，性能参差不齐”，仅一次销售仅售出 6,255 英镑。其余的都被遗弃了。

一项涉及出售给 Lords 旗下马里波恩板球俱乐部 (Marylebone Cricket Club) 的饮料设备的和解协议，所得收益为 62,000 英镑。

您是受此影响的 Brewdog 债权人或工人吗？它产生了什么影响？

母公司 BrewDog PLC 仍预计将全额支付其优先债权人 HMRC 所欠的 366 万英镑税款——主要是增值税和消费税。

Brewdog 最大的债务是金融服务集团汇丰银行 (HSBC)，其各个银行部门欠汇丰银行 (HSBC) 的债务超过 6100 万英镑。

它已收回数千万英镑，但仍面临估计 1680 万英镑的缺口。

报告指出，这可以通过在美国出售资产来减少。

私募股权支持者 TSG 于 2017 年收购了该啤酒厂 22% 的股份，预计将损失 2760 万英镑。

Brewdog 还欠无担保债权人约 1.9 亿英镑。他们预计收到的款项不到一便士。

Brewdog 倒闭导致 38 家英国酒吧立即关闭

3 月，美国公司收购了 Brewdog 的品牌和英国业务后，裁减了 440 名员工，并将 736 名员工转移到 Tilray。

裁员人员可以通过政府破产服务机构索取拖欠工资。 AlixPartners 表示，工人们已获得有关此支持的信息。

作为出售的一部分，11 家酒吧被保留，而其他 38 家酒吧则立即关闭。

Brewdog的倒闭也让约20万名众筹投资者的股票变得一文不值。

今年早些时候，Alixpartners 证实，朋克股权计划的投资者不会获得股票回报。

投资者通常会花费约 500 英镑购买股票——尽管其他人投资的金额要大得多——以换取公司股份、折扣和福利。

管理人员表示，这些股票现在“没有价值”。

Brewdog 由好友 James Watt 和 Martin Dickie 于 2007 年创立，鼎盛时期在全球拥有四家啤酒厂和约 100 家酒吧。

瓦特表示，倒闭后他“心碎”，并向员工和投资者道歉。

我们已联系 Brewdog 的主人 Tilray 征求意见。
